root_cause.text: In `ttm_bo_shrink()` the TTM LRU/bulk-move bookkeeping removed a buffer object from the bulk-move list before calling `ttm_tt_backup()`, so if backup failed the BO stayed on the shrinkable LRU path and could be selected again in an endless LRU walk.
root_cause.evidence: The patch moves `ttm_resource_del_bulk_move(bo->resource, bo)` from before `ttm_tt_backup()` to after successful backup only, replacing the failure-path `ttm_resource_add_bulk_move()` with `ttm_resource_del_bulk_move_unevictable()` and `ttm_resource_move_to_lru_tail()`, and the commit message explicitly says it fixes an “infinite LRU walk on backup failure” in `ttm_bo_shrink()`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Adjust TTM shrink handling to update bulk-move and LRU state only after successful backup, moving the object to the unevictable LRU tail.
intent_record.what: The code no longer removes the buffer object from the bulk-move list before calling ttm_tt_backup(). Instead, after ttm_tt_backup() returns, the code now checks for lret > 0 and, under lru_lock, calls ttm_resource_del_bulk_move_unevictable(bo->resource, bo) followed by ttm_resource_move_to_lru_tail(bo->resource). The previous post-backup re-add to bulk move was removed.
intent_record.how: This changes the ordering of LRU/bulk-move bookkeeping so it only occurs when backup succeeds with a positive return value. It prevents the object from being prematurely removed and then restored in the old way, and instead updates its state to unevictable and moves it to the tail of the LRU, affecting reclaim/eviction behavior after successful backup.

grouping_result.intent: Adjust TTM shrink handling to update bulk-move and LRU state only after successful backup, moving the object to the unevictable LRU tail.

relevance_review.reason: The change matches the root cause: it fixes TTM shrink bookkeeping so the BO is only removed from bulk-move / moved on the LRU after tt m_tt_backup() succeeds, preventing the object from remaining on the shrinkable LRU path after a backup failure.

candidates.rationale: This removed the BO from the bulk-move list before `ttm_tt_backup()` ran. If backup later failed, the object had already been taken out of the bulk-move bookkeeping even though it remained shrinkable, which is the core cause of the endless LRU walk.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement removed the buffer object from the bulk-move bookkeeping before `ttm_tt_backup()` completed. If backup later failed, the BO remained on the shrinkable LRU path but was no longer tracked in bulk-move state, allowing it to be selected again in an endless LRU walk.

bic_trace_step.reason: The snippet shows the exact vulnerable pattern: when `bo->bulk_move` is set, the buffer object is removed from the bulk-move list before backup is attempted: `ttm_resource_del_bulk_move(bo->resource, bo);` at lines 1103-1106, followed only later by `lret = ttm_tt_backup(...)` at lines 1109-1111. If backup fails, the object is only re-added when `lret <= 0` at lines 1113-1116, which matches the root cause described (removal before `ttm_tt_backup()` can leave the BO on the shrinkable LRU path and lead to repeated selection). There is no evidence here of the later fix preventing that bookkeeping issue, so `is_fixed` is false.
